title: The Weird Circle
paragraphs: A supernatural and mystery anthology built largely from adaptations of classic literature by writers such as Edgar Allan Poe and other authors of Gothic, macabre, and fantastic fiction.
Transcribed New York literary horror/mystery anthology of 78 programs, distributed in syndication rather than as one simultaneous nationwide network schedule.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: Transcribed literary-horror anthology package (1943 to 1945).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Ted Jewett (announcer), Peggy Mayer (writer), Alan Devitt (performer), Alfred Shirley (performer), Burford Hampden (performer), Walter Vaughn (performer), and Edwin Jerome (performer).

The stories often return to supernatural and uncanny forces, death, murder and mortality, Gothic houses, ruins and confinement, ghosts and hauntings, madness, obsession and unstable perception, and curses and fatal objects.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Transcribed syndication model, Classic-literature adaptation culture, Wartime-era escapist horror anthology, and AFM recording ban and The Weird Circle music-free sound.

The stories often return to supernatural and uncanny forces, death, murder and mortality, Gothic houses, ruins and confinement, ghosts and hauntings, madness, obsession and unstable perception, and curses and fatal objects.
